Stout ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0001-9470-1032 4 , 5 na1 , David Kaplan ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-9245-7774 1 , 4 , 5 & … Rodrigo Ledesma-Amaro ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0003-2631-5898 1 , 2 , 3 , 6 Show authors Nature Biotechnology volume 44 , pages 1811–1823 ( 2026 ) Cite this article Save article View saved research 918 Accesses 1 Altmetric Metrics details Abstract Cellular agriculture promises to reduce the environmental burden and inefficiencies of food systems. The question is no longer whether precision fermentation and cultivated meat production can produce alternative proteins and other food components, but whether they can attain the cost, scale and quality required for broad adoption. We examine cellular agriculture through the interrelated lenses of enabling technologies, food function and manufacturing economics. The field is approaching an inflection point where biological technology development is less important for commercial success than achieving scalable, affordable manufacturing. Key challenges include how products and their functional attributes are designed and how production processes are configured. For precision fermentation, the most compelling opportunities lie in functional approaches to improve taste, nutritional quality, health benefits and formulation rather than in direct imitation of existing foods or ingredients. For cultivated meat production, impact will come first from hybrid and ingredient-based products that capture specific values of cellular ingredients while avoiding the costs of full tissue mimicry.
